_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden pep). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. FOCUSED REBUILD (2026-09-05): installed from an owner-supplied rewrite (audit/tool-notes/PEP-NOTES.md) that reduces the prior FULL V2 REWRITE's five modes (Right Now/Prioritize/Week/Patterns/Adapt, 17 actions) down to ONE loop across 3 actions: generate (Right Now menu), just-do-this (single suggestion, no menu), reflect (log what happened). Prioritize/Week/Patterns/Adapt/Shared menu/Match/build-a-plan are GONE, not renamed — do not resurrect their schema keys chasing a 'completeness' instinct. New schema: generate={read,top_pick:{activity,why_it_fits,first_step,duration,done_when},alternatives:[{activity,why_it_fits,duration}],history_note}; just-do-this={activity,why_it_fits,first_step,duration,done_when,history_note}; reflect={reflection,history_observation}. LIVE-CAUGHT BUG, fixed same day: the SYSTEM prompt's own 'avoid absolutes about effort' rule listed the banned phrases ('zero effort, no attention, no decisions, completely passive') as a literal example list, and the model echoed them back near-verbatim on the FIRST test call ('This requires zero setup, zero decisions, and zero physical effort') — the model was handed a copyable bad-phrase template and copied it. Fixed by describing the constraint without listing the banned words as an example set. The validateResult() regex backstop ALSO missed this on the first pass — its 260-char/2-sentence cap (meant to spare a long paragraph from being nuked over one incidental match) let a 3-sentence field with a genuine, repeated 'zero X' violation straight through; raised to 400 chars/3 sentences. Both fixes verified together: re-ran the exact failing input, output came back clean ('asks very little... no setup, no goal, no output' — describing fit, not claiming zero demand). The generate-low-energy-evening-screens case captured here IS that exact regression input — re-running it and finding a 'zero setup/effort/decisions/attention' phrase anywhere in the output is the bug back. DO NOT reintroduce: any of the removed modes' schema keys; a prompt rule that lists banned phrases as a literal copyable example set (describe the constraint, don't hand over the phrase); the tight 260/2 validateResult cap (400/3 is the corrected value). SECOND live-caught bug, same day: a visitor screenshot showed the top_pick activity title rendered one word per line in a collapsed column — root cause was 'duration' holding a full clause ('20 minutes lying still, leaving 10 minutes to sit up, reorient, and prepare for your call.') instead of a short time span; the flex row's whitespace-nowrap duration span demanded its full single-line width and starved the title's share of the row. Fixed at three layers: (1) prompt now explicitly caps duration at ~4 words with an example; (2) a shortenDuration() backstop in validateResult() extracts the leading time span or cuts at the first clause break, deterministically, regardless of prompt compliance; (3) the frontend Activity card gives the title flex-1 min-w-0 and caps the duration span at max-w-[40%] instead of an unbounded whitespace-nowrap sibling, so even an unexpectedly long duration can no longer collapse the title. All three cases here were re-captured after the fix — every duration value is now a short span (e.g. '10–15 minutes'). DO NOT reintroduce whitespace-nowrap on that duration span, and do not let 'duration' drift back into a descriptive clause. FINAL FOCUSED TOOL CORRECTIONS pass, same day: just-do-this's schema DROPPED why_it_fits entirely — 'Just tell me what to do' must feel noticeably simpler than the full menu (one activity, one first step, one stopping point, no analysis paragraph, no alternatives). The just-do-this-no-menu-wanted case here has no why_it_fits key at all; do not add it back. Also this pass: history now speaks at the activity level first ('you rated these two lying-down activities 7/10 each') rather than inventing abstract categories ('stillness is your recharge pattern') from 1-2 data points; a before/after rating change is described as N-points-higher, never as what the activity 'gave' or 'raised'; history_note/history_observation are genuinely optional now — populated only when history changed the answer, empty otherwise (both recorded cases show this: empty when nothing relevant, non-empty in live tests when it materially mattered); 'show me different' explicitly excludes the avoid list rather than paraphrasing it; My Menu and What I've Tried stay structurally distinct on the frontend — rating an activity no longer auto-adds it to My Menu (see src/tools/PEP.js submitReflection). Two new validateResult() regex categories added (observed-rating-change-as-caused-effect, unsupported-pattern-generalization-from-sparse-history), and the effort-absolutes category widened after a live catch of 'asks nothing of you' — a phrasing not covered by the original zero/no-paired-with-setup pattern. TIME_META's 'All evening' (daypart) replaced with 'open-ended' (duration) — a daypart mixed into a duration row broke the mental model.

input.context: Been staring at screens all day, doom-scrolling between meetings. A hike sounds awful right now.

output.read: You've been on screens all day with doom-scrolling on top of meetings, and you have almost nothing left. The pick below asks very little of you.

top_pick.activity: Lie down with your eyes closed — no phone, no audio
top_pick.why_it_fits: You're at home, have 15 minutes, and a 2/10 with a numb mood points toward something that needs barely any setup or decision-making. This one asks only that you find a surface to lie on and set a timer. No screen, no input, no choices after that.
top_pick.first_step: Put your phone face-down, set a 15-minute timer, then lie down wherever is closest — bed, couch, floor.

alternatives.activity: Sit somewhere away from your screens with a warm drink
alternatives.why_it_fits: If lying down flat doesn't appeal, this gets you off screens with very little effort — just move to a different chair or spot, make or grab something warm, and sit with it until it's gone.

input.context: Meeting in 10 minutes and I cannot decide anything else right now.

output.activity: Sit still and look out a window or at a blank wall
output.first_step: Put your hands in your lap and let your eyes settle on something that isn't a screen
output.done_when: When the meeting starts — you have a hard stop already built in

input.note: Felt better once I was outside

output.reflection: You rated this 8/10 for helpfulness, and your energy went from 3 to 6 — a 3-point rise. You noted feeling better once you were outside.
